title: B2+ · L20 — Idioms: time
description: Idioms sobre el tiempo: in the nick of time, against the clock, time flies, y otros esenciales.

questions.prompt: Le cuentas a un amigo como alcanzaste el vuelo justo antes de que cerraran la puerta.
questions.question: 'We arrived just in the nick of time' means:
options: We arrived far too late.
We arrived at the very last possible moment.
We arrived unusually early.
We arrived injured with a small cut.
questions.explanation: 'In the nick of time' = justo a tiempo, en el ultimo instante posible antes de que fuese demasiado tarde. Idiom antiguo (nick = punto exacto marcado en un palo de calculo medieval). Muy comun en narrativa dramatica: rescates, plazos, deportes. Registro: neutro, informal-narrativo. Error hispano frecuente: omitir 'the' ('in nick of time' es incorrecto) o traducir literal 'en el corte del tiempo'. Colocacion fija: siempre 'in THE nick of time', nunca 'at' o 'on'.
examples: The paramedics got there in the nick of time — a few minutes later and we'd have lost him. → drama medico
We caught the last train in the nick of time — literally jumped in as the doors were closing. → anecdota casual

questions.prompt: El SRE explica al PM por que no puede dar estimacion precisa: llevan 3 horas trabajando en un outage.
questions.question: 'We're working against the clock' means:
options: We're repairing a broken clock.
We're under intense time pressure with a hard deadline.
We're moving in a clockwise direction.
We're deliberately ignoring the deadline.
questions.explanation: 'Against the clock' = contrarreloj, con presion temporal maxima. Muy comun en emergencias, deadlines apretados, deportes de tiempo. Se combina naturalmente con 'race' ('racing against the clock' es la forma mas dramatica). Colocacion 'up against the clock' anade urgencia. Error hispano: traducir 'against' como opuesto adversarial — aqui es mas neutro (el reloj no es el enemigo, solo la restriccion). Registro: neutro-formal; comun en business, engineering, journalism.
examples: The whole team is racing against the clock to fix the outage before customers wake up in Europe. → crisis SRE
We're up against the clock to submit the RFP before midnight — nobody's going home. → deadline corporativo

questions.statement: 'Time flies when you're having fun' means time seems to pass quickly during enjoyable moments.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Refran universal, tambien acortado a 'time flies' cuando el contexto es obvio. Refleja fenomeno psicologico real: el tiempo subjetivo se acelera cuando estamos absortos (flow state). Uso conversacional cotidiano en despedidas ('is it midnight already?'), reuniones ('has it been an hour?'), o reflexiones vitales ('the kids are grown up already'). Registro: neutro, coloquial. Error hispano: usar 'flies' en singular con sujeto plural — 'time' es incontable aqui, siempre 'flies'.
examples: Wait, it's already midnight? Time really does fly when you're having fun. → despedida casual
Can't believe it's been ten years working here — time flies. → reflexion en aniversario laboral

questions.prompt: Un amigo te pregunta cuando visitaste por ultima vez cierto restaurante.
questions.question: 'That was ages ago' means:
options: That was very recently.
That was an extremely long time ago.
That will happen tomorrow.
That was during a historical age.
questions.explanation: 'Ages ago' = hace muchisimo tiempo. Hiperbole coloquial — puede ser semanas, meses o anos dependiendo del contexto y dramatismo. Muy comun en habla oral casual. Colocaciones: 'in ages' ('I haven't seen him in ages'), 'take ages' ('this is taking ages'). Diferencia sutil UK vs US: en UK 'ages' es MUY frecuente en todo contexto; en US se prefiere 'forever' ('I haven't seen you in forever'). Error hispano: traducir literal como 'edades' — no funciona.
examples: I haven't been to that restaurant in ages — must be five years at least. → nostalgia casual
That was ages ago — I barely remember what I said. → esquivando responsabilidad amablemente

questions.text: We were pressed for time, so we had to cut a few corners to hit the deadline.
questions.explanation: Dos idioms de tiempo en frase profesional confesional. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'pressed for' con /stf/ cluster consonantico, la /d/ final de 'pressed' se elide dejando /prestfɔːr/ en habla natural. 'Cut a few' con catenacion /kʌtəˈfjuː/ (t-flap en US). Colocaciones fijas: 'pressed for time' (con poco tiempo, sin margen), 'cut corners' (hacer atajos sacrificando calidad — connotacion negativa), 'hit the deadline' (cumplir el plazo). Error hispano: 'cut corners' se traduce como 'atajar', no como 'cortar esquinas'.
examples: I'm a bit pressed for time — can we make this quick and pick up the details later? → excusa educada
Don't cut corners on QA even if we're pressed for time — the bugs will bite us later. → advertencia senior

questions.prompt: Tu pareja te pregunta si haras la reserva del restaurante para el sabado o dejaras el plan abierto.
questions.question: 'Let's play it by ear' regarding timing means:
options: Let's listen carefully to music.
Let's decide as we go, without a fixed plan.
Let's cancel all our plans.
Let's plan every detail rigorously.
questions.explanation: 'Play it by ear' = improvisar, decidir sobre la marcha en funcion de como evolucione la situacion. Metafora musical: tocar sin partitura, solo de oido. Uso ubicuo en planes flexibles (weekends, viajes, meetings). Registro: neutro, muy oral. Colocacion tipica en business: 'let's play the meeting by ear' (adaptaremos la agenda segun surja). Error hispano: traducir 'jugar de oido' — inentendible en espanol; equivale mas a 'improvisar' o 'ir viendo sobre la marcha'.
examples: Let's play it by ear on Saturday — see how the weather holds and decide in the morning. → plan flexible
I don't want to over-plan the trip — we'll play it by ear once we land. → viaje relajado

questions.prompt: Empareja cada idiom de tiempo con su traduccion al espanol:
questions.explanation: Set esencial de idioms de tiempo. 'At the eleventh hour' viene de la parabola biblica (Mateo 20:6-16) donde los trabajadores contratados en la undecima hora reciben el mismo pago — se ha fosilizado como sinonimo de 'ultimo momento'. 'Around the clock' se usa para servicio 24 horas, tipico en support, hospitales, monitoring. 'Call it a day' es especialmente comun al final de una jornada larga o proyecto agotador. Todos neutros US/UK.
examples: The deal came together at the eleventh hour — I thought it was dead until 11pm the night before signing. → drama de negociacion
Our SRE team runs around the clock, seven days a week, in three follow-the-sun shifts. → operacion global

questions.target: We're up against the clock, so let's call it a day at midnight and pick this up first thing tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Combina 'up against the clock', 'call it a day', y 'first thing tomorrow'. Discurso tipico de team lead en crunch mode que reconoce agotamiento y protege al equipo. Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras cada coma, tono descendente y firme en 'midnight' y 'tomorrow' (decision, no propuesta). Contracciones: 'we're', 'let's' obligatorias. 'First thing tomorrow' es colocacion fija (nunca 'first thing at tomorrow'). Registro: liderazgo profesional-empatico.
examples: It's been a long day, folks — let's call it a day and reset in the morning. Fresh eyes will help. → cierre empatico
We're at the eleventh hour, but we'll get there. Just push through the next two hours. → motivacion en crunch

questions.prompt: Un analista de seguridad advierte sobre una vulnerabilidad no parcheada.
questions.question: 'It's only a matter of time before X happens' means:
options: X will never happen.
X will definitely happen eventually, it's inevitable.
X might happen if we're unlucky.
X will happen in exactly one hour.
questions.explanation: 'A matter of time' = inevitable, cuestion de cuando (no de si). Se usa para predicciones fuertes o advertencias donde el evento se considera seguro. Colocacion fija: 'only a matter of time before...' es la forma completa mas comun. Registro: neutro-formal, comun en analysis, journalism, business planning. Error hispano: confundir con 'a question of time' — ambas existen pero 'matter of time' es la version anglo canonica. 'Question of time' se usa mas en UK.
examples: It's only a matter of time before someone tries to exploit that endpoint — we need to patch it now. → alerta de seguridad
It's a matter of time before the market corrects — this bubble can't hold forever. → prediccion economica

questions.statement: 'Better late than never' expresses that lateness is preferable to not doing something at all.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Refran universal para consolar o restar drama a un retraso. 'Better late than never' se usa cuando algo llega tarde pero se agradece igualmente: felicitaciones tardias, entrega tarde, disculpa tarde. Registro: neutro, coloquial-conversacional. En UK y US identico. Uso ironico frecuente: cuando alguien llega media hora tarde a una reunion, 'better late than never' puede ser suave reproche disfrazado de amabilidad — leer el tono es clave.
examples: Congrats on the promotion — sorry for the late text, better late than never! → felicitacion tardia
Finally read that book everyone recommended three years ago. Better late than never, I guess. → autoironico

questions.prompt: Tienes 3 horas de espera en un aeropuerto entre vuelos.
questions.question: 'To kill time' means:
options: To commit a violent act.
To fill empty time with a distracting activity.
To save time by working efficiently.
To waste time in a harmful way.
questions.explanation: 'Kill time' = pasar el tiempo mientras esperas algo, sin objetivo productivo, para no aburrirse. Registro NEUTRO, no negativo (a diferencia de 'waste time' que si tiene connotacion critica). Contextos tipicos: aeropuertos, salas de espera, entre reuniones. Colocacion: 'kill an hour', 'have time to kill'. Error hispano: sonar dramatico al traducirlo literalmente — es completamente neutro en anglo. Alternativa mas casual: 'kill a bit of time'; mas formal-eufemistica: 'pass the time'.
examples: I killed time at the bookstore while waiting for my connecting flight to Tokyo. → aeropuerto tipico
We've got two hours to kill before dinner — fancy a coffee somewhere? → propuesta casual

questions.text: We're running out of time — let's not drag our feet on this decision any longer.
questions.explanation: Dos idioms de tiempo en frase de urgencia profesional. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'running out of' con enlazado /rʌnɪŋaʊtəv/, y en habla rapida la /f/ final de 'of' casi se elide antes de 'time'. 'Drag our feet' con /grr/ dificil; la /r/ final de 'our' se enlaza con la /f/ inicial de 'feet' de forma catenativa. Colocaciones: 'run out of X' (agotarse X), 'drag one's feet' = demorarse deliberadamente, ser reluctante (connotacion negativa clara). Error hispano: 'drag one's feet' se traduce como 'arrastrar los pies' — funciona metaforicamente en ambos idiomas.
examples: We can't drag our feet on hiring — the window closes when Q2 planning starts. → urgencia de reclutamiento
Time's running out. Decision needed by EOD, no more circling. → ultimatum ejecutivo

questions.prompt: Le cuentas a un colega sobre una amiga a la que casi nunca ves.
questions.question: 'She saw him once in a blue moon' means:
options: She saw him under blue lighting.
She saw him very rarely, almost never.
She saw him extremely frequently.
She saw him only in the morning.
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' = muy rara vez, casi nunca. Metafora astronomica: 'blue moon' es la segunda luna llena en un mismo mes calendario, ocurre cada 2-3 anos. Registro: neutro-conversacional, ligeramente literario. Se usa para expresar infrecuencia extrema con toque poetico. Alternativas mas casuales: 'hardly ever', 'almost never', 'like never'. Curiosidad cultural: origen del titulo de la cancion 'Blue Moon' y de la frase 'happens once in a blue moon' viralizada en anglo global.
examples: I only eat dessert once in a blue moon — trying to stay off sugar. → habito raro
Rain like this happens once in a blue moon around here — usually it's just a light drizzle. → clima excepcional

questions.statement: 'To beat the clock' means to finish something before the deadline expires.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Beat the clock' = terminar antes del tiempo limite, ganarle al reloj. Connotacion positiva y triunfal (contraste con 'against the clock' que enfatiza la presion, no el resultado). Muy comun en deportes, exams, deadlines profesionales, videojuegos. Registro: neutro. Diferencia sutil con 'in the nick of time': 'beat the clock' celebra logro; 'in the nick of time' enfatiza dramatismo del ultimo momento. Frecuente en headlines periodisticas ('Team beats the clock to secure playoff spot').
examples: We submitted the bid and beat the clock by 15 minutes — cutting it fine but we made it. → cierre triunfal
You'll need to hustle to beat the clock on this one, the deadline's brutal. → advertencia motivacional

questions.target: We beat the clock in the nick of time — but honestly, we can't keep working around the clock like this.
questions.explanation: Tres idioms de tiempo encadenados de forma natural, no forzada: 'beat the clock', 'in the nick of time', 'around the clock'. Discurso de reflexion post-crunch: reconoce logro + advierte sobre insostenibilidad. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras el guion, tono descendente en 'in the nick of time', tono firme y grave en la advertencia. Contracciones: 'can't', obligatoria. 'Honestly' es discourse marker que anade autenticidad y transicion a la parte critica. Registro: liderazgo empatico, tipico de retro post-launch.
examples: We made the deadline in the nick of time, but at what cost to the team? → reflexion critica
Working around the clock isn't sustainable — even to beat the clock, we need a better rhythm. → propuesta de cambio
